Twenty tables, zero VLOOKUPs, one click to any people answer

Sterlite Power's HR numbers lived in separate extracts stitched together with VLOOKUPs. HMC connected them in one Power BI data model, moved every Excel calculation into Power Query (M) and DAX, and built a 12-page dashboard where every chart filters every other.

The Challenge

Disparate datasets held together by VLOOKUPs

Headcount, CTC, joining and relieving data came from different sources. Every monthly review meant rebuilding the joins in Excel, and every chart was a static picture of one cut.

Disparate datasets

HRMS extracts, CTC sheets, compa data and joining and relieving trackers, each with its own keys and layout.

VLOOKUP chains

Dozens of lookup columns copied down every row: slow to recalculate and broken by a single inserted column.

Static charts

Charts did not talk to each other. Answering "what about Finance, M4 and above?" meant a new pivot.

Repeated working

Age bands, tenure groups, fiscal months and attrition were recalculated by hand each cycle.

HMC Approach

Model first, visuals second

Built with Sterlite Power's HR team, so the model matches how they already think about people.

Select a step to see what happened.

Discover · Map every lookup

Traced the Excel working end to end.

  • Listed each source file, its key and refresh cadence.
  • Catalogued every VLOOKUP and helper column.
  • Agreed the questions leadership asks every month.

Deliverable: Source and lookup inventory.

Design · A star schema

One fact table, many small dimensions.

  • Fact_Report at employee grain, active and exited.
  • Dimensions for age, grade, tenure, function, BU, location, CTC and attrition reason.
  • Sort-order columns so bands display in the right order.

Deliverable: Model diagram and relationship plan.

Build · M, DAX and visuals

Every Excel step rebuilt where it belongs.

  • Power Query (M) for cleaning, typing and derived columns.
  • DAX measures for headcount, diversity, attrition and cost.
  • A dynamic fiscal-month measure so YTD numbers annualise themselves.

Deliverable: 12-page Power BI report.

Adopt · Use it in the review

The dashboard replaced the Excel pack.

  • Landing page with tiles for each area.
  • Slicers for business unit, function and location.
  • HR team trained to refresh and extend it.

Deliverable: Refresh guide and walkthrough.

Scale · Add questions, not files

New analysis plugs into the same model.

  • New pages reuse the same measures.
  • New source columns flow through M automatically.
  • Talent management pages added on the same model.

Deliverable: Extensible model.

    Key Takeaways

    What any HR team can borrow

    01

    Relate, don't look up

    A relationship replaces a VLOOKUP column on every row, and it never breaks when a column moves.

    02

    Put logic where it belongs

    Shape data in M, calculate in DAX, and leave Excel as a source, not a calculator.

    03

    Interactivity is a model feature

    Cross-filtering comes free once every chart sits on the same model.
